name: TMP1075DGKR
title: Digital temperature sensor with I2C/SMBus interface, LM75 pinout
summary: A digital temperature sensor that reads its own die temperature with a 12-bit converter (0.0625 °C per count) and reports it over a two-wire I2C/SMBus interface. It is pin- and software-compatible with the LM75 and TMP75, is accurate to ±1 °C max over -40 °C to 110 °C (D and DGK), and has an ALERT output with programmable high and low limits. The TMP1075 comes in SOIC-8, VSSOP-8 and WSON-8 for 1.7 V to 5.5 V; the TMP1075N is a SOT563 version for 1.62 V to 3.6 V with one address pin.
key_figures: ±0.25 °C typ, ±1 °C max (-40 °C to 110 °C, D and DGK), ±2 °C max (-55 °C to 125 °C)
10 µA typ at 27.5 ms conversion period; 2.7 µA typ at 220 ms
I2C/SMBus, 400 kHz fast mode, 2.56 MHz high-speed mode; 32 addresses

notes: D is SOIC-8, DGK is VSSOP-8 and DSG is WSON-8, all TMP1075; DRL is the 6-pin SOT563 of the TMP1075N.
The TMP1075N differs in supply range (1.62 V to 3.6 V), temperature range (-40 °C to 125 °C), accuracy band, number of addresses (4), and has no conversion-rate setting and no device ID register.
Nominal package sizes including leads: VSSOP 3.00 mm × 4.90 mm, SOIC 4.90 mm × 6.00 mm, WSON 2.00 mm × 2.00 mm, SOT563 1.60 mm × 1.60 mm.

circuits.title: Typical connections
circuits.description: The sensor on a host's two-wire bus. Three 5 kΩ resistors pull SDA, SCL and ALERT up to the supply, and a 0.01 µF capacitor bypasses V+ to ground. A0, A1 and A2 are all tied to ground, which sets the 7-bit address 1001000. The TMP1075N has no A1 or A2 pin and runs from 1.62 V to 3.6 V instead of 1.7 V to 5.5 V.

parts.value: Supply, 1.7 V to 5.5 V (TMP1075), 1.62 V to 3.6 V (TMP1075N)

notes: A1 and A2 are absent on the TMP1075N.

equations.name: Temperature from the register

where.T[11:0]: bits 15:4 of the temperature register read as a 12-bit two's-complement number

equations.note: The same scale applies to the low and high limit registers.

operation.text: An on-chip bipolar transistor senses temperature and a 12-bit ADC converts it. Heat reaches the die through both the package leads and the plastic body; the metal leads, with the lower thermal resistance, are the main path.

Each conversion lands in a read-only 16-bit register: the upper 12 bits hold the result in two's complement and the lower 4 bits are zero. The low byte can be skipped when the fraction below 1 °C is not wanted. It reads 0 °C from power-up or reset until the first result is ready.

The part is a target on an I2C/SMBus bus, with Schmitt-trigger inputs and spike filters on SDA and SCL. It supports fast mode to 400 kHz and high-speed mode to 2.56 MHz (2.85 MHz on the TMP1075N); bytes go most significant bit first. It never drives SCL.

A0 and A1 each take one of four states (GND, V+, SDA or SCL) and A2 one of two (GND or V+), giving 32 addresses from 1000000 to 1011111. The TMP1075N has only A0, for four addresses from 1001000 to 1001011. The pins are sampled at every bus transaction, so they must be settled before the bus is used.

The first byte after the address in a write sets the pointer, whose low bits choose the register; further bytes in the same write are stored in that register. A read returns the register the pointer last selected, high byte first, so repeated reads of one register need no new pointer write. To read another register the host writes only the pointer byte, then issues a repeated START with the read bit set. The pointer resets to 00h. The host ends a read with a not-acknowledge, a START or a STOP.

operation.topic: One-byte access to the configuration register
operation.text: For code written for xx75 sensors, a single-byte write to the configuration register sets bits 15 to 8 and a single-byte read returns those bits. On the TMP1075N only single-byte reads and writes are to be used with the configuration register.

In interrupt mode ALERT can act as an SMBus alert line. When the host sees it asserted it sends the alert response address (0001 1001); every part with ALERT active acknowledges and returns its own address. The address byte's last bit equals POL when the alert came from reaching THIGH and the inverse of POL when it came from falling below TLOW. If several parts answer, address arbitration decides: the winner releases ALERT at the end of the response, and a loser keeps ALERT asserted. In comparator mode the alert response is ignored.
The part acknowledges the general-call address (0000 000 with the R/W bit 0). If the next byte is 0000 0110 it loads all its registers with their power-up values.

To go above 400 kHz the host first sends the high-speed host code 00001XXX after a START. The part does not acknowledge it but switches its SDA and SCL input filters and SDA output filter to high-speed operation, and stays there until it sees a STOP, when it returns to fast-mode filtering.
A 50 ns spike filter on SDA and SCL lets the part share a mixed fast-mode bus with I3C devices clocked up to 12.5 MHz without being disturbed by their traffic.

When the host keeps SCL low, or the part keeps SDA low, for 25 ms typical (30 ms on the TMP1075N) between START and STOP, the interface resets, releases SDA and waits for a new START. Keeping the bus clock at 1 kHz or faster avoids triggering it.

With SD = 0 the part repeats a cycle of one active conversion (5.5 ms; 10 ms on the TMP1075N) followed by standby. R1:R0 set the cycle length to 27.5, 55, 110 or 220 ms; the TMP1075N is fixed at 250 ms. Current is high during the conversion and low in standby, so a longer period lowers the average current.

Setting SD = 1 powers down everything except the serial interface. In shutdown, writing 1 to OS runs one conversion and returns the part to shutdown. On the TMP1075 OS always reads 0; on the TMP1075N it reads 0 while the conversion runs and 1 once it has finished.

ALERT asserts once the temperature has been at or above THIGH for the number of consecutive conversions set by F1:F0, and releases once it has been below TLOW for the same count. The gap between the limits is the hysteresis, and the fault count rejects noise.

ALERT asserts after the fault count of readings at or above THIGH and stays asserted until one of three events clears it: any register read, the part winning an SMBus alert response, or entering shutdown. The part then watches for readings below TLOW, asserts again after the fault count, waits for another clearing event and goes back to comparing against THIGH. On the TMP1075, changing TM, entering shutdown or a reset clears this history.

POL = 0 (default) makes ALERT active low and POL = 1 active high. On the TMP1075 any write to TM deasserts ALERT and clears the fault count and interrupt history, and ALERT can be kept from ever asserting by setting TLOW to -128 °C and THIGH to +127.9375 °C.

After reset the TMP1075 converts continuously every 27.5 ms, ALERT is in active-low comparator mode with a fault count of 1, TLOW is 75 °C (4B00h) and THIGH is 80 °C (5000h). The device ID register reads 7500h. Power-on reset releases at 1.22 V typical on a rising supply; brown-out detection trips at 1.1 V typical.

5 kΩ is the suggested pull-up value; other values work as long as the current into SCL and SDA stays at or below 3 mA. SCL, SDA, A0 and A1 may be pulled to a rail above V+; so may ALERT on the TMP1075. A2 connects only to GND or V+. An unused ALERT pin may be grounded or left open. SCL needs a pull-up only when the host drives it open drain.

Put the part close to the heat source it is to watch, with good thermal coupling, so changes reach it quickly. For air or surface measurement the package and leads should be shielded from the surrounding air; a thermally conductive adhesive helps for surface readings. A ground plane under GND that reaches the heat source carries the heat to the part.

A bypass capacitor, typically 0.01 µF, goes as close to V+ and GND as possible; noisy or high-impedance supplies may need more. To keep self-heating down and precision up: run from the lowest rail available, keep the bus quiet during conversions, use one-shot mode, drive bus lows near ground and highs above 90 % of V+, keep bus rising edges under 1 µs with pull-ups below 10 kΩ, and tie A0 and A1 to GND or V+.
The SOIC, VSSOP and WSON parts match the xx75 pinout, and the 16-bit registers accept single-byte reads and writes, so existing xx75 code runs unchanged.
